## Overview

`DEGreports` is a modular RNA-seq differential expression pipeline built on
DESeq2. You can run **everything in one call**, or call **each stage on its
own** and assemble the HTML report at the end.

Two one-command entry points:

| Function | When to use |
|---|---|
| `run_deseq2()` | Group contrasts (1–3 factors; pairwise / main effects / interactions) |
| `run_deseq2(mode = "lrt")` | Time-course / ordered trajectory (LRT + degPatterns clusters) |
| `run_deg()` | Precomputed **merged DEG table** (no counts); GSEA / TF / PPI / HTML |

(`run_deseq2()` remains as a **deprecated alias** of `run_deseq2()`.)

Modules cover quality control, sample distance/PCA, differential expression,
GSEA (Wald / DEG-table) or cluster ORA (LRT), STRING PPI, CSPA surface
markers, optional GSVA / WGCNA / decoupler-tf / decoupler-ccc / VIPER, cross-analysis
gene hits, and a multi-page HTML report.


Companion vignettes:

- **[Module reference](degreports-modules.html)** —
  `vignette("DEGreports-modules", package = "DEGreports")`
- **[Analysis flow](degreports-analysis-flow.html)** —
  `vignette("DEGreports-analysis-flow", package = "DEGreports")`

Organism (human/mouse) is auto-detected from gene symbols via
`detect_organism()` -- there is no `org` argument. Row names should be
standard HGNC/MGI symbols (not Ensembl/Entrez IDs). Use
`summarize_genes_dds()` / `load_nfcore()` when you start from transcript- or
Ensembl-level counts.

## Loading a DESeqDataSet

From a count matrix:

```{r}
library(DEGreports)
library(DESeq2)

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts,
  colData = coldata,
  design = ~ condition
)
```

From an **nf-core/rnaseq** `.RData` + `tx2gene` TSV (collapses features that
share a gene symbol):

```{r}
dds <- load_nfcore(
  rdata = "salmon.merged.gene_counts.RData",
  tx2gene = "tx2gene.tsv"
)
```

Or attach symbols yourself and collapse:

```{r}
rowData(dds)$gene <- gene_symbols
dds <- summarize_genes_dds(dds, gene_sym_col = "gene")
```

## One-command Wald pipeline

```{r}
out <- run_deseq2(
  dds = dds,
  var = "condition",
  filter_method = "cpm",
  cpm_percentile = 0.05,
  ranking = "log2FoldChange",
  collections = c("HALLMARK", "GOBP", "REACTOME"),
  run_gsva = TRUE,
  run_wgcna = TRUE,
  run_decoupler_tf = TRUE,
  run_decoupler_ccc = TRUE,
  run_viper = TRUE,
  render_html = TRUE,
  save_dir = "results"
)
```

Under `results/` this writes per-module folders plus `index.html`:

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `qc/` | Sample QC + library QC + PCA page (`qc.html`); `counts/` and `distance/` subfolders |
| `deseq2/` | Per-contrast DE tables & plots, CSPA (`<contrast>/cspa/`), PPI (`<contrast>/ppi/`), hub `deseq2.html` |
| `clusterprofiler/` | Per-contrast GSEA (+ overlap), hub `clusterprofiler.html` |
| `gsva/` | Sample GSVA scores / heatmaps (if `run_gsva = TRUE`) |
| `wgcna/` | Modules, ORA, per-module `ppi/`, `wgcna.html` (if `run_wgcna = TRUE`) |
| `decoupler-tf/` | CollecTRI/ULM, `decoupleR-TF.html` (if `run_decoupler_tf = TRUE`) |
| `decoupler-ccc/` | LIANA/ULM ligand–receptor, `decoupleR-CCC.html` (if `run_decoupler_ccc = TRUE`) |
| `viper/` | bcellViper/VIPER, `viper.html` (if `run_viper = TRUE`) |
| `multihit/` | Cross-analysis top genes + `multihit.html` (own nav tab) |
| `ppi/` | STRING PPI for LRT temporal clusters (`<cluster>/ppi/`; contrast PPI under `deseq2/`) |
| `logs/` | Timestamped run log + JSON session record |

Local CollecTRI priors under `inst/extdata/collectri_{human,mouse}_*.csv`
(shipped with the GitHub install; auto-downloaded from the repo if missing)
are used automatically before OmniPath.

## One-command LRT pipeline

For ordered time / trajectory designs, use `run_deseq2(mode = "lrt")`:

```{r}
out <- run_deseq2(
  mode = "lrt",
  dds = dds,
  var = "genotype",       # or NULL for time-only
  time = "day",
  include_interactions = TRUE,
  run_gsva = TRUE,
  run_wgcna = TRUE,
  run_decoupler_tf = TRUE,
  run_decoupler_ccc = TRUE,
  run_viper = TRUE,
  save_dir = "results_lrt"
)
```

LRT mode fits nested full/reduced models, clusters significant genes with
**degPatterns**, runs **ORA** (not ranked GSEA) per cluster, scores TFs per
cluster, and writes per-cluster multihit tables to the **Multihit** HTML page.

## One-command DEG-table pipeline

When you already have differential-expression results (no raw counts), pass a
**merged** table with a `comparison` column:

```{r}
# Required columns: gene, comparison, log2FoldChange, padj (or pvalue)
# Example comparison labels: "groupA_vs_groupB", "groupA_vs_groupC"
out <- run_deg(
  deg_table = "all_contrasts_deg.csv",
  collections = c("HALLMARK", "GOBP"),
  run_decoupler_tf = TRUE,
  run_decoupler_ccc = TRUE,
  run_viper = TRUE,
  save_dir = "results_from_deg"
)
```

This runs GSEA, GSEA leading-edge overlap, CSPA marker tables (no VST heatmap),
contrast-level ULM / msVIPER, DEG PPI, multihit ranking, and HTML. QC, WGCNA,
and sample-level TF heatmaps are skipped. See `?prepare_diffexp_from_deg` for
column aliases.

## Modular usage (Wald)

Each stage is a standalone function with the same arguments the pipeline uses:

```{r}
dds_qc <- run_qc(dds, var = "condition", filter_method = "cpm",
                 save_dir = "results/qc")
distance_out <- run_distance_pca(dds_qc, var = "condition",
                                 save_dir = "results/distance")
diffexp_out <- run_diffexp_pipeline(dds_qc, var = "condition",
                                    shrinkage = "ashr",
                                    ranking = "log2FoldChange",
                                    save_dir = "results/deseq2")
gsea_out <- run_gsea_pipeline(
  diffexp_out$results,
  collections = c("HALLMARK", "GOBP", "REACTOME"),
  ranking = "log2FoldChange",
  save_dir = "results/clusterprofiler"
)

# Optional modules …
wgcna_out <- run_wgcna_pipeline(dds_qc, var = "condition", save_dir = "results/wgcna")
decoupler_tf_out <- run_decoupler_tf_pipeline(
  dds_qc, var = "condition", diffexp_out = diffexp_out,
  save_dir = "results/decoupler"
)
viper_out <- run_viper_pipeline(
  dds_qc, var = "condition", diffexp_out = diffexp_out,
  save_dir = "results/viper"
)
ppi_out <- run_ppi_pipeline(
  diffexp_out = diffexp_out, wgcna_out = wgcna_out,
  save_dir = "results/deseq2",
  module_save_dir = "results/ppi",
  wgcna_module_save_dir = "results/wgcna"
)
cspa_out <- run_cspa_marker_pipeline(
  dds_qc, diffexp_out = diffexp_out, save_dir = "results/deseq2"
)
multihit_out <- run_multihit_pipeline(
  diffexp_out, gsea_out = gsea_out,
  viper_out = viper_out, decoupler_tf_out = decoupler_tf_out,
  cspa_out = cspa_out, save_dir = "results/multihit"
)

render_report(
  dds = dds_qc, var = "condition",
  distance_out = distance_out, diffexp_out = diffexp_out,
  gsea_out = gsea_out, multihit_out = multihit_out,
  wgcna_out = wgcna_out, decoupler_tf_out = decoupler_tf_out,
  viper_out = viper_out, ppi_out = ppi_out, cspa_out = cspa_out,
  save_dir = "results"
)
```

## Two- and three-factor designs

With two or three grouping columns, every factor's **main effect** is tested:
its pairwise (and, with ≥ 3 levels, one-vs-rest) comparisons across all levels
of the other factors. So for `var = c("v1", "v2", "v3")` you get
`v1l1_vs_v1l2+v1l3` regardless of `v2` and `v3`, `v2l1_vs_v2l2` regardless of
`v1` and `v3`, and so on. These are fitted on every sample with an additive
design (`~ [batch +] [pair +] other factors + tested factor`), so the factors not under
test are adjusted for rather than left in the residual. The design is additive
and the labels flat:

```{r}
out <- run_deseq2(
  dds,
  var = c("Tissue", "Isotype"),
  save_dir = "results_2factor"
)
```

`include_interactions = TRUE` switches the design to the full product
(`~ A * B`, `~ A * B * C`) and adds **difference-of-differences** contrasts to
the main effects. Each asks whether one factor's effect differs between two
levels of another — "does the K effect differ between C and noC, within CB" —
which is the same question as "does the C effect differ between K and noK,
within CB", so each factor pair contributes one contrast per stratum rather
than two:

```text
deseq2/C_vs_noC/C_vs_noC_diffexp.csv     # main effect: C vs noC, all celltypes and K states
deseq2/C_vs_noC_x_K_vs_noK_in_CB/...     # C x K interaction within CB
deseq2/CC_vs_CB_x_K_vs_noK_in_C/...      # celltype x K interaction within C
deseq2/CC_vs_CB_x_C_vs_noC_x_K_vs_noK/…  # three-way: does C x K differ between CC and CB
```

Every interaction contrast is a combination of coefficients from **one** fit of
the product design on all samples, so they share the dispersion estimates and
sample size of the main effects. A factor with three or more levels is compared
one-vs-rest rather than pairwise (`CA_vs_CB+CC_x_K_vs_noK_in_C`: does the K
effect differ between CA and the average of CB and CC, within C), which keeps
the grid linear in the number of levels and matches how that factor's main
effects read. The pooled side is a mean of coefficients — each level weighted
`1/(k - 1)` regardless of its sample count — fitted from a numeric weight
vector over `resultsNames()`. Two-level factors keep the pairwise direction of
**factor level order** (non-reference vs reference), not alphabetical sorting.

The hub page (`deseq2.html`) lists every interaction row with the question it
answers and what a positive `log2FoldChange` means for it, since a difference
of differences is easy to misread as a plain group comparison.

```{r}
out <- run_deseq2(
  dds,
  var = c("celltype", "C_mutation", "K_mutation"),
  include_interactions = TRUE,   # main effects + interaction contrasts
  save_dir = "results_3factor"
)
```

## Paired designs

When the same donor, patient or animal is measured under each condition, name
that column in `pair`. It is added to every model as a blocking term, so each
comparison is made within donors:

```{r}
# coldata: donor = d1 d1 d2 d2 d3 d3 ..., condition = Control Treated ...
out <- run_deseq2(dds, var = "condition", pair = "donor",
                  save_dir = "results_paired")
# design: ~ donor + condition   (with batch: ~ batch + donor + condition)
```

The donor effect is also removed from the PCA, sample-similarity heatmap and
sample-level modules with `limma::removeBatchEffect()`. Every tested factor
must vary within donors: a factor that is constant within every donor (e.g.
genotype when each donor has one genotype) cannot be estimated in a paired
design and is reported as an error. Donors seen in only one condition trigger
a warning, since they add nothing to the within-donor comparison. `pair` works
the same way in `run_limma()` and `run_deseq2(mode = "lrt")`.

## Imputed sex

`run_qc()` imputes each sample's sex from the sex-chromosome marker genes on
every run (after low-expression filtering, before any X/Y gene removal) and
stores it as `colData(dds)$imputed_sex`. The pipeline adds it to every model
when it is not confounded with `var`, `pair` or `batch`; the QC page says
whether it was used. A single-sex cohort is reported as undetermined and sex
is left out. Call `impute_sample_sex(dds)` to run the step on its own.

## Customising the comparisons

Every run writes `deseq2/contrasts.csv` and shows the same table at the top of
the DESeq2 page: one row per contrast, with the question it asks in prose, the
design formula actually fitted for it, the number of samples that model sees,
and the coefficients it combines. Read it first — it is the record of what was
compared.

Comparisons can be narrowed, extended, or written from scratch.

1. **Inspect the grid before running it.** `expand_contrast_specs()` returns
   the table the pipeline would use, and `contrast_manifest()` turns it into
   the same manifest the run writes.
2. **Run a subset.** Pass the labels you want as `comparisons`; anything in
   the grid can be named.
3. **Add a contrast the grid does not generate.** Build it with
   `contrast_spec()` (levels) or `contrast_spec_from_coefs()` (model
   coefficients), append it with `add_contrasts()`, and pass the table.
4. **Fit a one-off contrast outside the pipeline.** `run_diffexp_coef()` takes
   coefficient names or a weight vector directly.

```{r}
# 1. what would run?
specs <- expand_contrast_specs(dds, var = c("Tissue", "Isotype"))
contrast_manifest(specs, dds, var = c("Tissue", "Isotype"))

# 2. a subset of the grid
out <- run_deseq2(dds, var = c("Tissue", "Isotype"),
                       comparisons = c("SP_vs_BM", "IgG_vs_IgM"),
                       save_dir = "results_subset")

# 3. a pooled-vs-pooled comparison the grid never emits, plus a hand-written
#    coefficient contrast, appended to the automatic grid
grid <- add_contrasts(
  specs,
  contrast_spec(
    label      = "earlyIso_vs_lateIso",
    test_var   = "Isotype",
    comparison = "IgM+IgD_vs_IgG+IgA",
    question   = "Do the early isotypes differ from the class-switched ones?"
  ),
  contrast_spec_from_coefs(
    label    = "SP_specific_IgG_effect",
    weights  = c(TissueSP.IsotypeIgG = 1),
    question = "Does the IgG effect differ between SP and BM?"
  )
)
out <- run_deseq2(dds, var = c("Tissue", "Isotype"), comparisons = grid,
                       include_interactions = TRUE, save_dir = "results_custom")

# 4. outside the pipeline entirely
res <- run_diffexp_coef(dds, coef_weights = c(TissueSP.IsotypeIgG = 1,
                                              TissueLN.IsotypeIgG = -0.5,
                                              TissueBM.IsotypeIgG = -0.5))
```

A single grouping factor also accepts any well-formed comparison of its levels
directly — `comparisons = "d0+d1_vs_d7+d14"` — without building a spec table.
With two or more factors, a label that is not in the grid is an error naming
the valid labels, so a typo cannot silently become a different contrast; use
`contrast_spec()` when you mean it.

`stratified = TRUE` adds the within-stratum contrasts: each factor compared
inside one fixed level combination of the others, fitted on that subset alone.
An interaction contrast asks the same question with every sample behind it, so
these stay opt-in — reach for them when the strata are not expected to share a
dispersion.

### Settings

`opts = degreports_opts()` holds the statistical and per-module settings —
shrinkage estimator, `alpha`, the LFC cutoff, the per-module top-N budgets.
The defaults are the values the entry points apply by default, so runs stay
comparable; only settings you change are listed in the report's "Pipeline
arguments" table.

```{r}
out <- run_deseq2(
  dds, var = "condition",
  opts = degreports_opts(alpha = 0.01, lfc_threshold = 1),
  save_dir = "results_strict"
)
```

## Example runners

In the package source tree:

```bash
Rscript --vanilla run_gse189410_deseq2_wald.R    # single-factor isotype (Wald)
Rscript --vanilla run_gse189410_deseq2_lrt.R     # isotype as time axis (LRT)
```

## Reading the HTML report

Open `results/index.html` from the results folder (share the whole tree,
including `lib/` and per-module CSVs). Pages use `self_contained = FALSE`
with relative cross-links and on-disk CSV links. Nav order:

`Index` → `QC` → `DESeq2` → `clusterProfiler` → `GSVA` → `WGCNA` → `decoupleR-TF` → `decoupleR-CCC` →
`VIPER` → `Multihit`.

Notable report sections:

- **QC**: Sample QC (detected genes / total transcripts) → Library QC →
  PCA (scatter, scree, loadings, PC–covariate association heatmap) →
  sample similarity.
- **DESeq2 / clusterProfiler hubs**: summary tables of significant
  up/down DEGs or pathways (n and %), then links to per-contrast pages.
- **Multihit**: own page after VIPER (not embedded on the index).

Each report section shows the **minimal package call** needed to reproduce
that module's results.
